rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT method (plane‑wave, BEEF‑vdW) combined with the computational hydrogen electrode approach. Non‑trivial to implement correctly (building defect‑graphene models, applying ZPE/entropy corrections, mapping energies to catalytic descriptors), but the underlying theory is well‑established and the paper does not introduce a brand‑new formalism.
rationale.execution: Multi‑stage pipeline: (1) generate 7×7 graphene vacancy models with metal/N dopants, (2) run spin‑polarized DFT geometry optimizations for bare and three adsorbate states per model (~16 jobs), (3) parse total energies and apply corrections, (4) derive CO desorption barriers and HER limiting potentials. Requires careful environment setup (Quantum ESPRESSO, pseudopotentials) and robust data handoffs between stages, but the workflow is linear and the output is simple JSON.
